mcq_choices.rationale: Mistakenly assumes conduction requires generating new charge carriers rather than freeing the already-present ions to move.
charge carriers are fixed in the solid lattice but mobile in the melt
Assumes melting converts the ionic lattice into covalent molecules, but NaCl remains fully ionic in the melt.
Assumes the chloride ion must lose its negative charge to conduct, when ionic charge is unchanged by melting.

parts.prompt:
Why does solid NaCl not conduct while molten NaCl does?

A. Electrons are created on melting
B. Ions become mobile on melting
C. NaCl becomes molecular
D. Chloride loses its charge

criteria.description: Select the single scientifically correct answer.
required_evidence: charge carriers are fixed in the solid lattice but mobile in the melt

review_notes.expected_reasoning: charge carriers are fixed in the solid lattice but mobile in the melt
